paragraphs: Unsupervised translation attempts to connect languages without examples showing how particular messages translate. This paper asks what can be established when the problem is harder still: the two collections of communication need not discuss similar subjects or share similar linguistic structure. Animal communication motivates this broader theoretical setting.

The authors develop a framework for studying this problem and apply it to two simplified models of language. For these models, they prove bounds on the amount of data needed and check the theoretical results using synthetic data. This connects translation difficulty to properties of the communication systems, rather than assuming the similarities that make human-language translation easier.

The bounds associate lower error with greater language complexity and more common ground between the systems. Within this framework, complexity can therefore help make translation possible. The results suggest that sufficiently complex animal communication might support unsupervised translation; they do not establish successful translation of an actual animal communication system.
neurips-2023-a-theory-of-unsupervised-tr.tldr: A theoretical framework suggests that unsupervised animal communication translation may be feasible when communication is sufficiently complex.

paragraphs: Gradual domain adaptation uses intermediate datasets to help a model move from its original data distribution to a different target distribution. This paper examines adversarial robustness in that setting. It modifies gradual self-training, where a model supplies labels for unlabeled examples and then learns from those predictions.

The proposed method follows pseudo-labeling with adversarial training on the resulting distribution. The authors find improvements in both adversarial accuracy and accuracy on unmodified target examples. Their explanation centers on mistakes in the predicted labels: adversarial training can handle these imperfect training signals better than standard training in the setting studied.

The theoretical analysis provides generalization bounds for multiclass gradual adaptation. It uses the optimal value of a Subset Sum Problem to relate ordinary error on the true distribution to adversarial error on the pseudo-labeled distribution. The resulting comparison indicates that adversarial training may yield a tighter bound when pseudo-labels are incorrect. A conditional Gaussian example further explains how improved clean accuracy can arise.
neurips-2023-adversarial-self-training-i.tldr: Adversarial self-training improves robustness and clean target accuracy in gradual adaptation, with theory linking the gains to imperfect pseudo-labels.

paragraphs: AV-NeRF studies how to generate a matching visual and auditory experience from viewpoints absent from an original recording. Given a video of an audio-visual scene, the goal is to create new videos with spatial sound along novel camera trajectories. Moving the viewpoint therefore requires synthesizing both what is seen and what is heard.

The approach builds on neural radiance fields and adds an audio generation component informed by sound propagation. This implicitly links generated sound to the environment's geometry and material properties. A second component transforms coordinates so that viewing direction is expressed relative to the sound source, allowing the model to learn acoustic fields organized around that source.

The authors also collect the Real-World Audio-Visual Scene dataset to support this task. Evaluations on that dataset and the simulation-based SoundSpaces dataset demonstrate advantages for the proposed method. The contribution combines a scene synthesis task, a model connecting visual structure with acoustics, and real-world data for evaluating whether generated sound and imagery agree.
neurips-2023-av-nerf-learning-neural-fie.tldr: AV-NeRF connects visual scene structure with acoustic modeling to synthesize matching imagery and spatial sound from new viewpoints.

paragraphs: Functional Diffusion Processes extend score-based diffusion modeling to spaces of functions with infinitely many dimensions. The central change is to formulate generation around continuous functions. This requires describing how those functions evolve during both the forward diffusion process and the backward process used for generation.

The paper develops mathematical tools that make this formulation usable for training. An infinite-dimensional version of Girsanov's theorem supports computation of an evidence lower bound, a training-related quantity. An extension of the sampling theorem establishes the equivalence between functions and their evaluations at a countable set of points within the framework. These steps connect the infinite-dimensional description to quantities a practical model can handle.

The resulting generative models do not require specialized neural architectures and are designed to handle continuous data. In experiments on real data, the authors report high-quality image generation using a simple multilayer perceptron with orders of magnitude fewer parameters than existing diffusion models. This demonstrates that the function-space formulation can support compact image generators.
neurips-2023-continuous-time-functional-.tldr: Functional Diffusion Processes extend diffusion to infinite-dimensional function spaces and demonstrate high-quality image generation with compact, simple networks.

paragraphs: Time-sequential data can contain harmonic structure that naturally admits complex-valued representations. Spectral kernels use frequency-related parameters to model this structure, including statistical patterns that change over time. The paper argues that discarding the imaginary component, as many existing methods do, restricts what these representations can express.

CosNet preserves complex-valued information through two connected modules. The first extends spectral kernel mappings from real numbers to complex numbers, allowing real-valued observations to receive complex-valued representations. The second combines those spectral kernels with neural networks to capture relationships across long intervals or recurring periods. Together, the modules make complex spectral structure part of the learned representation.

The authors analyze the approach through bounds on covering numbers and generalization error, examining the theoretical effects of the expanded mapping. Experiments report better performance than mainstream kernel methods and complex-valued neural networks. The contribution is therefore both representational and architectural: it retains information dropped by earlier spectral methods and integrates that information into a neural model.
neurips-2023-cosnet-a-generalized-spectr.tldr: CosNet retains complex-valued spectral information and combines it with neural networks to model long-range and periodic relationships.

paragraphs: A reinforcement learning network can gradually become less able to learn from new experience, a phenomenon called loss of plasticity. Identifying its effects is difficult because learning ability, exploration, and task performance interact. A stalled agent could have several problems, so its score alone does not clearly identify the cause.

The paper introduces plasticity injection, a small intervention that increases learning flexibility without changing the number of trainable parameters or biasing predictions. It also serves as a diagnostic: if performance improves after injection, the authors argue that the network had been losing plasticity. Applying this test identifies a subset of Atari environments where reduced plasticity causes performance plateaus.

The intervention also has practical uses when exhausted plasticity would otherwise force an agent to learn again from scratch. The paper considers improving training efficiency and dynamically growing an agent's network without compromising performance. Atari results show stronger performance than alternative methods alongside computational efficiency, supporting plasticity injection as both an investigative tool and a training intervention.
neurips-2023-deep-reinforcement-learning.tldr: Plasticity injection restores learning flexibility and helps diagnose when lost plasticity causes reinforcement learning performance to plateau.

paragraphs: Language-guided object recognition can use descriptions containing color, shape, and relationships, but providing those details does not ensure a model interprets them. The authors find that GLIP often relies strongly on object names while overlooking contextual information. This limits the value of richer queries for recognizing unfamiliar objects.

DesCo changes the learning approach so that descriptions become meaningful supervision. It uses a large language model to generate detailed object descriptions from commonsense knowledge. It also introduces context-sensitive queries intended to make the recognition model attend to descriptive context rather than depend on names alone. The two components address both the availability of rich descriptions and the model's ability to use them.

Under zero-shot detection, the method reports 34.8 APr minival on LVIS and 29.3 AP on OminiLabel, with respective reported improvements of 9.1 and 3.6. These results exceed the prior methods GLIP and FIBER in the stated evaluations. The findings support training explicitly for description interpretation as a way to improve recognition of novel objects.
neurips-2023-desco-learning-object-recog.tldr: DesCo improves zero-shot object detection by training models to interpret rich descriptions instead of relying mainly on object names.

paragraphs: Auditing group fairness normally requires knowing which sensitive groups people belong to. That information may be unavailable even when a model is used for consequential decisions. This paper studies how to estimate and control violations of equalized odds in that situation, using predictors of sensitive attributes.

The first contribution is a set of computable upper bounds that tightly characterize the worst possible equalized-odds violation. Tightness matters because the bounds describe the worst case precisely, rather than merely providing a loose warning. The second contribution is a post-processing correction with a guarantee for controlling this worst-case fairness violation.

The analysis also determines when enforcing equalized odds using predicted group membership is optimal for worst-case control and when it is not. This distinction matters because predicted attributes are not interchangeable with known attributes for this purpose. The results hold under assumptions described as milder than those in previous work, and experiments on synthetic and real datasets illustrate the theoretical conclusions.
neurips-2023-estimating-and-controlling-.tldr: The paper provides tight fairness-violation bounds and a corrective method when sensitive attributes must be predicted rather than observed.

paragraphs: One-shot channel simulation asks how to encode a single sample from a target distribution using a coding distribution while keeping the average message short. It has applications in neural compression and differential privacy. The paper addresses the computational obstacles that have made existing solutions too slow or too restricted for wider use.

The proposed algorithm, greedy Poisson rejection sampling, connects rejection sampling with a greedy search over points of a Poisson process. This connection provides the basis for several algorithm variants whose correctness and running time the authors analyze. The central optimal-runtime result applies to one-dimensional problems where the ratio of target density to proposal density is unimodal, meaning it has a single mode.

Experiments verify the theoretical results and show substantial performance improvements over A* coding, the comparison method identified in the abstract. The significance is a computationally optimal solution within the stated one-dimensional, unimodal-ratio setting. The paper pairs that guarantee with empirical evidence that the construction can outperform an existing channel-simulation algorithm in practice.
neurips-2023-greedy-poisson-rejection-sa.tldr: Greedy Poisson rejection sampling achieves optimal runtime for one-dimensional channel simulation with a unimodal target-to-proposal density ratio.

paragraphs: Diffusion image models learn to reconstruct images from corrupted versions, often supervising individual pixels or features. The paper argues that this can leave predicted points insufficiently connected to their surroundings. ConPreDiff adds a training task that explicitly asks each point to predict information about its neighborhood.

A context decoder is attached to the ends of diffusion denoising blocks during training. It predicts neighboring pixels or features at multiple strides, encouraging each location to preserve semantic relationships with nearby content. The decoder is removed for inference, so the additional training machinery introduces no extra parameters into the sampling procedure. The framework is designed to apply to both discrete and continuous diffusion backbones.

Experiments cover unconditional image generation, text-to-image generation, and image inpainting. The authors report consistent improvements over previous methods, including a zero-shot FID of 6.21 on MS-COCO and a new state-of-the-art text-to-image result in their evaluation. The findings support neighborhood prediction as useful supervision that improves generation without retaining an additional decoder during sampling.
neurips-2023-improving-diffusion-based-i.tldr: ConPreDiff improves diffusion image generation with neighborhood prediction during training, then removes the added decoder for sampling.

paragraphs: Providing a graph neural network with distances does not ensure it can distinguish different geometric structures. The authors construct families of symmetric geometric graphs that ordinary distance-based message passing cannot tell apart, even when every pairwise distance is available. These examples expose limitations in how the network processes geometry.

The proposed k-DisGNN models extract richer geometric information from the distance matrix. The authors show that these models can learn higher-order information missed by the ordinary approach and encompass some existing geometric architectures. They also establish universal approximation results for scalar outputs when k is at least two and vector outputs when k is at least three.

These results connect geometric learning with expressive graph representation methods originally developed for other graph tasks. They show that complicated equivariant architectures are not the only available route to strong geometric models. Experiments support the theoretical analysis, and k-DisGNNs obtain multiple state-of-the-art results on MD17. The central lesson is that the architecture's use of distances matters alongside the distances themselves.
neurips-2023-is-distance-matrix-enough-f.tldr: Higher-order k-DisGNNs exploit distance matrices more expressively than ordinary message passing, with approximation guarantees and strong MD17 results.

paragraphs: Personalizing a text-to-image model for a new concept can require lengthy training even with adaptation methods intended to be efficient. This paper investigates whether that training continues after useful learning has largely finished. It examines the learning dynamics of approaches including Textual Inversion and DreamBooth.

The authors observe that most concepts are learned early and do not improve in quality later, while standard convergence measures fail to reveal this. They propose a simple early-stopping rule based on evaluating the usual training objective on a fixed collection of inputs throughout training. Holding those inputs fixed provides the basis for tracking the objective's evolution and deciding when to stop.

Experiments use Stable Diffusion with 48 concepts and three personalization methods. The proposed stopping approach achieves competitive results while making adaptation up to eight times faster, without significant quality drops in the reported evaluation. Its practical contribution is a drop-in way to reduce unnecessary training using the existing objective, rather than requiring a separate personalization method.
neurips-2023-is-this-loss-informative-fa.tldr: Tracking training loss on fixed inputs enables earlier stopping and up to eightfold faster image-model personalization without significant quality loss.

paragraphs: Evaluating medical imaging AI requires diverse cases, including combinations of patient and imaging characteristics that may be difficult to obtain. This paper proposes generating such cases through simulated imaging pipelines. Digital anatomical models, with and without disease, are passed through a digital replica of an imaging system to produce realistic synthetic images.

The authors release M-SYNTH, a mammography dataset covering four distributions of breast fibroglandular density and multiple exposure levels. The images are generated with Monte Carlo x-ray simulation using the VICTRE toolkit. This construction supports comparative evaluation across controlled variations in anatomy, lesion characteristics, and imaging exposure.

In the synthetic evaluation, AI performance decreases as breast density rises and improves as mass density rises. Lower exposure levels also reduce performance, while the highest observed performance occurs below the nominal recommended dose for the breast type. These are findings about model behavior in the simulated evaluation. The dataset's contribution is to make such systematic comparisons possible when corresponding patient cases are not readily available.
neurips-2023-knowledge-based-in-silico-m.tldr: M-SYNTH uses simulated mammography to evaluate how AI performance varies with breast density, mass density, and imaging exposure.

paragraphs: Tree-search planning with learned models has succeeded in settings such as Go and Atari, but extending it to broader decision problems is challenging. Complex action spaces, costly simulation, and randomness all complicate the design. LightZero introduces a unified benchmark for studying MCTS and MuZero across more varied sequential decision settings.

The work identifies central obstacles to a general tree-search solver and separates tightly connected algorithmic and system components into distinct modules. The authors then improve these components using exploration and optimization strategies suited to the task. This modular approach makes the design of a search-based learning agent an explicit part of the benchmark.

The resulting agents are evaluated across board games, Atari, MuJoCo, MiniGrid, and GoBigger. Detailed benchmark results indicate substantial potential for building efficient, scalable decision systems with these methods. The contribution combines a common evaluation framework with improved agents spanning several domains, providing evidence that learned-model tree search can apply more broadly than its most familiar successes.
neurips-2023-lightzero-a-unified-benchma.tldr: LightZero provides a modular benchmark and improved agents for applying MCTS and MuZero across diverse sequential decision tasks.

paragraphs: This paper studies sequential games in which multiple competing players interact through a network. At each state, the associated game has zero-sum payoffs and a separable structure across neighboring players. The framework captures local interactions while retaining a structured form of competition.

The authors characterize exactly when a Markov game admits this representation. They also establish a relationship between equilibrium concepts: taking each player's per-state marginal from a Markov coarse correlated equilibrium and forming their product yields a Markov Nash equilibrium. Despite this relationship, finding approximate stationary coarse correlated equilibria in infinite-horizon discounted games is PPAD-hard unless the network has a star topology.

For star-shaped networks, the paper develops fictitious-play-style learning dynamics and proves convergence to stationary Nash equilibria. It also studies non-stationary equilibria, providing finite-iteration guarantees for value-iteration-based algorithms. Numerical experiments support the theoretical findings. The results distinguish the consequences of network structure and whether strategies must remain stationary, showing why these choices matter for equilibrium computation.
neurips-2023-multi-player-zero-sum-marko.tldr: The paper characterizes equilibria and computational difficulty in networked zero-sum Markov games, with stronger stationary guarantees for star networks.

paragraphs: NetHack poses a difficult learning problem because it combines long-term decisions, an open-ended environment, and multiple forms of observation. In the referenced challenge, symbolic agents achieved more than four times the median score of neural approaches. This paper investigates the gap through a detailed study of neural policy learning.

The authors instrument the winning symbolic agent to record its internal strategy choices and generate a large demonstration dataset. They use those demonstrations to examine action hierarchies, neural architecture improvements, and combinations of imitation learning with reinforcement learning. Recording strategy selection allows the study to consider the organization of behavior alongside individual actions.

The resulting neural agent improves median game score over previous fully neural policies by 127% in offline settings and 25% in online settings. Nevertheless, the study finds that scaling alone does not close the gap with the strongest symbolic agents or top human players. The work therefore delivers substantial neural-policy improvements while identifying an unresolved challenge in learning long-horizon behavior.
neurips-2023-nethack-is-hard-to-hack-6a1.tldr: Demonstrations and policy-design improvements substantially strengthen neural NetHack agents, but scaling alone does not close the symbolic-agent performance gap.

paragraphs: Empirical risk minimization selects a model by minimizing loss on observed data, yet its mean squared error can fall short of the minimax rate. This paper separates that error into bias and variance. Under relatively mild assumptions, it proves that the variance term achieves the minimax rate, so any rate suboptimality must arise from bias.

The authors give an elementary probabilistic proof for fixed design and extend the argument to various random-design models. They also simplify a proof of an admissibility result, under which empirical risk minimization cannot be ruled out as optimal in the fixed-design setting, and extend that result to random design. Their estimates additionally imply stability results for non-Donsker classes.

A final result reveals an irregular relationship between prediction-space proximity and empirical loss in the non-Donsker regime. Functions can be close to an empirical risk minimizer in L2 distance while remaining far from nearly minimizing the training loss. Together, the findings distinguish variance control, admissibility, and local loss behavior instead of treating them as equivalent forms of quality.
neurips-2023-on-the-variance-admissibili.tldr: Under relatively mild assumptions, empirical risk minimization's variance achieves the minimax rate, making bias responsible for any rate suboptimality.

paragraphs: In social-network experiments, a person's outcome can depend on treatments assigned to connected people. This interference makes estimating the global average treatment effect difficult. Earlier designs often preserved unbiasedness by trimming substantial amounts of data, which could produce high estimation variance.

The paper instead explicitly balances bias and variance under a potential-outcome model with one-hop interference. It derives how both terms for the standard Horvitz-Thompson estimator depend on network structure and the covariance of treatment assignments. The experimental design problem then becomes choosing that covariance matrix to minimize the estimator's mean squared error.

The authors provide an efficient projected gradient descent algorithm for implementing the desired randomization scheme. Simulation studies compare the method with existing approaches across many settings, including different degrees of model misspecification, and demonstrate advantages. The contribution is to treat dependence among treatment assignments as a design variable, using the modeled network effects to balance systematic estimation error against variability rather than optimizing unbiasedness alone.
neurips-2023-optimized-covariance-design.tldr: The method optimizes treatment-assignment covariance to balance bias and variance in social-network A/B tests with one-hop interference.

paragraphs: Seal transfers knowledge from vision foundation models into models for segmenting automotive point-cloud sequences. Its pretraining procedure directly distills visual knowledge into point clouds without requiring either 2D or 3D annotations. This offers a way to obtain useful point-cloud representations from existing visual models.

The framework enforces spatial and temporal relationships at two stages: transferring information from cameras to LiDAR and regularizing relationships between points and segments. These constraints support consistent learning across sensing modalities and across a sequence. The resulting representations can transfer to downstream point clouds spanning real and synthetic data, different resolutions and scales, and clean or corrupted inputs.

Experiments cover eleven point-cloud datasets. With linear probing, Seal reaches 45.0% mIoU on nuScenes, with reported margins of 36.9 over random initialization and 6.1 over prior approaches in mIoU. It also improves results across 20 few-shot fine-tuning tasks on the tested datasets. These findings support the usefulness of the transferred representations both with limited downstream adaptation and when only a small amount of task-specific data is available.
neurips-2023-segment-any-point-cloud-seq.tldr: Seal distills vision foundation models into point-cloud representations without pretraining annotations and improves segmentation across diverse datasets.

paragraphs: The original StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge became a widely used benchmark for cooperative reinforcement learning, but strong scores may overstate the need for responsive coordination. This paper shows that a policy using only the current timestep can obtain non-trivial win rates in many scenarios. Such a policy does not adjust its actions to observations.

The authors attribute this weakness to insufficient randomness and partial observability, then introduce SMACv2 to address it. Procedurally generated scenarios require agents to handle previously unseen settings drawn from the same distribution during evaluation. An additional extended partial observability challenge makes restricted information a meaningful part of the task.

The analysis shows that these changes require closed-loop policies that respond to observations. Evaluations of state-of-the-art algorithms reveal challenges absent from the original benchmark. SMACv2 therefore changes what successful performance demonstrates: agents must adapt their behavior within varied scenarios, rather than succeeding through action patterns that can be chosen solely from elapsed time.
neurips-2023-smacv2-an-improved-benchmar.tldr: SMACv2 adds generated scenarios and meaningful partial observability so cooperative agents must respond to observations to succeed.

paragraphs: Unsupervised domain adaptation transfers a model to a target domain with a different data distribution. The paper argues that methods emphasizing similarity between domains can overlook relationships within each domain, empirically weakening the ability to distinguish categories. SPA aims to preserve useful internal structure while making transfer possible.

The approach represents the adaptation problem using graphs. A coarse alignment mechanism and a spectral regularizer align domain graphs in their eigenspaces, bringing graph structure into the matching process. A finer message-propagation module then uses neighbor-aware self-training to improve discrimination in the target domain. These components address alignment between domains and relationships among examples together.

Experiments on standardized benchmarks report performance beyond existing leading domain-adaptation methods. Additional model analysis supports the authors' claims of stronger robustness, discrimination, and transferability. The contribution is a graph-based way to address the tension between making domains compatible and keeping their examples distinguishable, with coarse structural alignment complemented by local propagation during target-domain learning.
neurips-2023-spa-a-graph-spectral-alignm.tldr: SPA combines spectral graph alignment with neighbor-aware self-training to improve transfer while preserving target-domain discrimination.

paragraphs: Microcontrollers have limited working memory and slow processors, making neural-network inference difficult. Processing small patches instead of entire tensors reduces peak SRAM use, but conventional patch-based inference repeats substantial computation. The memory savings can therefore come with a costly increase in multiply-accumulate operations.

StreamNet introduces a stream buffer to eliminate redundant computation in patch-based inference. It supports both one-dimensional and two-dimensional streaming, and includes an algorithm that automatically chooses parameters to improve performance while requiring little SRAM space. The design directly addresses the interaction between memory usage and computation, which is especially consequential on constrained microcontrollers.

Across ten TinyML models, StreamNet-2D achieves a geometric-mean speedup of 7.3 times and reduces multiply-accumulate operations by 81% relative to the stated leading patch-based inference method. These results show that patch processing need not retain the same large computational penalty in the evaluated models. The contribution is an inference strategy that combines streaming with automatic parameter selection to make memory-efficient execution substantially faster.
neurips-2023-streamnet-memory-efficient-.tldr: StreamNet removes redundant patch computation, delivering a 7.3-fold geometric-mean speedup across ten TinyML models with low SRAM requirements.

paragraphs: TensorNet is a message-passing neural network for molecular systems that respects O(3) symmetry, including rotations and reflections. Its central design choice is to represent atoms using Cartesian tensors. This gives the model structured geometric features while simplifying feature mixing through ordinary matrix products.

The architecture can efficiently separate these tensors into components corresponding to scalars, vectors, and tensors. Those components can then be processed separately when needed. The approach combines symmetry-aware representation with relatively simple operations, aiming to reduce the cost of learning molecular quantities without giving up geometric structure.

Compared with higher-rank spherical tensor models, TensorNet reports state-of-the-art performance with substantially fewer parameters and reduced computational cost. For small-molecule potential energies, that performance can be achieved with a single interaction layer. The framework also allows accurate prediction of vector and tensor molecular quantities alongside energies and forces. These findings present Cartesian tensor embeddings as an effective design option for efficient equivariant molecular models.
neurips-2023-tensornet-cartesian-tensor-.tldr: TensorNet uses Cartesian tensor embeddings to achieve strong equivariant molecular predictions with fewer parameters and lower computational cost.

paragraphs: Choosing a useful similarity measure for time series is difficult, especially with small datasets. Reservoir computing offers a way to compare sequences through the dynamics that generate them, but its performance depends strongly on hyperparameters. Those settings can be difficult to interpret and expensive to optimize because the model is recurrent.

The paper constructs a time-series kernel using an established equivalence between reservoir dynamics and nonlinear vector autoregressive processes. The resulting kernel is non-recurrent and uses a small collection of meaningful hyperparameters. The authors also propose a heuristic for choosing them, addressing the practical burden of tuning as well as the structure of the representation.

Evaluations across a broad range of real-world classification tasks report strong accuracy and speed. The contribution extends nonlinear vector autoregression into kernel design for representing real-world sequences. It also clarifies how ideas from reservoir computing can support a representation that avoids recurrent computation while retaining a connection to the underlying dynamics of time-series data.
neurips-2023-time-series-kernels-based-o.tldr: A non-recurrent time-series kernel uses nonlinear autoregressive representations to deliver strong classification performance with a small, interpretable tuning space.

paragraphs: An image restoration model can be uncertain about coordinated changes across many pixels. A heatmap of separate pixel variances does not capture those relationships. This paper instead represents uncertainty through principal components of the posterior distribution, which describe directions of variation among plausible restored images.

One way to obtain these components is to generate many conditional samples and apply principal component analysis, but this is slow with diffusion samplers. The proposed method predicts posterior principal components in a single neural-network forward pass. It can be attached to a pretrained model optimized for mean squared error, or trained from scratch to predict both the restored image and the uncertainty components.

The authors demonstrate the approach on denoising, inpainting, super-resolution, and biological image translation. They report uncertainty estimates comparable to posterior sampling while running orders of magnitude faster. The predicted directions adapt to the individual input, making correlated uncertainty available without generating a large collection of restored images at test time.
neurips-2023-uncertainty-quantification-.tldr: A neural network predicts correlated image-restoration uncertainty in one forward pass, achieving sampler-comparable estimates orders of magnitude faster.
